items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-15
items.q: And from 9 to 1 or 1.30, you have Lou Saino. Lou Saino is at the Maison Bourbon now.

ctx.x: And now they have different bands. Now there's three five piece bands there now.

You have Tony Mitchell. Tony Mitchell and the Famous Door Five. And you have Thomas Jefferson and his Creole Jazz Band. And at night you have, well, in the midst of a change right now, Jim LaRocca's going in at night now. Tommy Yedda was there at night, but he left. And Jim LaRocca is related to Nick LaRocca in some way. I don't know whether he's son or uncle, one or the other. He's son. And what about Jimmy Isle? Where is he? Jimmy Isle moved down to the Maison Bourbon. He has the early shift there. They work…
The third reel is on now Bob.

items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-20
items.q: it's a photograph taken of Lou Saino, trombone player, who later went with the Louie Primer group

ctx.x: Oh, I couldn't think of Frank's name. All-round. Plays with circuses, too. When we're at his all-round guy. So now we have a celebrity with him here in this picture.

Well, back in the 30s and 40s and early 50s, you had quite a few celebrities that always came into the famous store every night. And this was shot, I don't know who shot this particular photograph. But anyway, it's a photograph taken of Lou Saino, trombone player, who later went with the Louie Primer group, traveled all around the country with Louie Primer for about 12 years before forming his own group and returning. Well, he did a little road work with his own group, Lou Saino, and then he is currently working…
I see a photograph here of Johnny Wig's band that you took yourself. You like to take photographs?
